policies.policy_name: Confirmed User Roles and Verified Record Relationships
policies.description: Before creating a parent‑child incident relationship, the assistant must ensure the request is based on a confirmed user role and that the relationship between the two incident records is verified.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on **confirmed user roles**, **verified record relationships**, and **ITIL/database integrity rules**.

policies.description: Both required parameters – parent_incident and child_incident – must be present; if either is missing, the operation must be halted and the missing field reported.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Only users whose role grants full CRUD access to Incidents (Administrator, Manager, or Agent) may invoke add_child_incident; a Reporter role is not permitted to modify incident relationships.
references: **Agent** (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | **Full CRUD** on **Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge**. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution.

policies.description: The add_child_incident tool must be called as a single, isolated operation; no other unvalidated actions may be combined in the same request.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform **one validated operation at a time**, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: The assistant must verify that both the parent_incident and child_incident IDs correspond to existing incident records before creating the mapping; IDs must not be fabricated or assumed.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.
When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.
